## Cincy Crashes

```{r API_connection}
httr2::request("https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/resource/rvmt-pkmq.json") |> # blue is the server, green is the path to one dataset on it; imputting the address
  httr2::req_url_query("$limit" = 5) |> # query parameters: after the ? come name=value paris that the documentation defines; $limit=5 asks for five rows
  httr2::req_perform() |> # only line that touches the network; everything before it only wrote the request; server checks validity of the request, then looks up five rows
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>  # gets you a response text body in form of json; status code first
  jsonlite::fromJSON() -> cincy_crashes # save into variable; converts JSON text into data frame
```


other query parameters:
$ limit - how many rows
$ order - sorted how
$ where - which rows
$ select - which columns

$ is part of the name on this server --> need it to avoid 400 (unrecognized arguments) error


anatomy of the url: https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/resource/rvmt-pkmq.json
- https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov: whose computer/data site
- /resource/rvmt-pkmq.json: path (endpoint) - which dataset on that server; rvmt-pkmq is the traffic crash table, .json is the format
- ?$limit=5&$order=crashdate DESC: query parameters (name=value) -- look at API documentation for parameters
- ? starts the question, & separates one parameter from the next


## Fred API Example

```{r fred}
httr2::request("https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations") |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    series_id = "IHLIDXUSOH",
    api_key = Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY"),
    file_type = "json"
  ) |> # will return a url with the API key and other requests
  # nothing has been sent yet
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON() -> ohio_jobs # list of 13 items, data is under the item "observations"



jobs_df <- ohio_jobs[[13]] # filter down to observations which is the last item in the list
# can do dplyr::glimpse(ohio_jobs) to view list values
# can do names(ohio_jobs) to get a list with indexes of the names


# to get data from Sept 1, 2026

# (a) to get all the data and then filter the rows that I want
## not the most efficient but correct
dplyr::glimpse(jobs_df)
jobs_df |> 
  dplyr::mutate( # need to set the date as a date; date was a character, overwrote it into a data column
    date = lubridate::ymd(date)  # must have tidyverse for this function
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(date >= '2026-09-01') -> jobs_df_mod

# (b) use the API since it had observation_start
httr2::request("https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations") |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    series_id = "IHLIDXUSOH",
    api_key = Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY"),
    file_type = "json",
    observation_start = "2026-09-01" # filter to start at september 9, 2026
  ) |> # will return a url with the API key and other requests
  # nothing has been sent yet
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON() -> ohio_jobs_sep_2026 # list of 13 variables

ohio_jobs_sep_2026_df = ohio_jobs_sep_2026$observations

```



## USA Jobs API

```{r usajobs}
httr2::request("https://data.usajobs.gov/api/search") |>
  httr2::req_url_query(Keyword = "Data Analyst", ResultsPerPage = 500) |>
  httr2::req_headers( # headers: name and value pairs that travel with teh request but are not part of the address (key goes here)
    Host = "data.usajobs.gov",
    "User-Agent" = "sanchedr@miamioh.edu",
    "Authorization-Key" = Sys.getenv("USAJOBS_API_KEY") # this site wants us to pass the API key as a header
  ) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON(flatten = TRUE) -> usa_jobs_list

# 401 error

usa_df <- usa_jobs_list$SearchResult$SearchResultItems

jobs_small = usa_df |>
  dplyr::select(
    title = MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle,
    department = MatchedObjectDescriptor.DepartmentName,
    agency = MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName,
    location = MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionLocationDisplay,
    closes = MatchedObjectDescriptor.ApplicationCloseDate
  )

```

```{r usajobs_questions}
## answer based on query
nrow(jobs_small)
# returns a named vector)
table(jobs_small$department) |>  sort(decreasing = T) |>  head(3)
# returns a df
jobs_small |>  dplyr::count(department) |>  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n)) |>  head(3)


index_data_analyst = jobs_small$title |> 
  stringr::str_detect(pattern = 'Data Analyst|Data Analytics')

jobs = jobs_small[index_data_analyst, ]
table(jobs$department)

```
